title: Power Automate: export work queue items to CSV from the automation center
summary: The briefing accurately reports the launched CSV download and its automatic availability. The documented security-role controls and Premium prerequisites check out, while export-specific settings, licensing and behaviour are appropriately identified as documentation gaps.

claims.claim: The automation center's work queues experience offers a download of work queue items as a CSV file.
claims.quote: You can now export work queue items directly from the Automation Center portal. A new option available in the Work Queues experience lets you download items as a CSV file.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes portable data for analysis, reporting or integration without external APIs or custom solutions.
claims.quote: This capability allows you to access work queue data in a portable format for further analysis, reporting, or integration with other tools, without needing to rely on external APIs or custom solutions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented which columns or how many rows this CSV download contains.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate work queue CSV download export license pricing meter request count limit columns audit scheduled. Opened automation-center-overview, work-queues-manage and work-queues-known-limitations; no CSV column list or row limit.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically described whether the CSV export applies the downloader's Dataverse privileges.
claims.quote: Searched: "automation center" "work queues" "export" "security". Opened automation-center-overview and work-queues-known-limitations: general data RBAC is documented, but no export-specific security behaviour is described.

claims.claim: No automated or scheduled mode is documented for this automation-center download option.
claims.quote: Searched: "work queue" "CSV" "export" "rollout" "scheduled". Opened automation-center-overview and work-queues-manage; no scheduled download. Search results describe unrelated exports and work queue processing.

claims.claim: The roadmap item states no licence requirement for the export.
claims.quote: This capability allows you to access work queue data in a portable format for further analysis, reporting, or integration with other tools, without needing to rely on external APIs or custom solutions.

claims.claim: Dataverse request limits cover read operations, including user-driven and internal requests from any client.
claims.quote: All create, read, update, and delete (CRUD), assign, and share operations including user-driven and internal system requests required to complete CRUD transactions, and special operations like share or assign. These operations can be from any client or application

claims.claim: Work queues are based on Dataverse and the same service protection and API limits apply.
claims.quote: Work queues are based on Dataverse technologies, hence the same service protection and API limits apply.

claims.claim: The Work Queue tab is unavailable in Dataverse for Teams environments, so this tab's export is not accessible there.
claims.quote: The Work Queue tab isn't available in Dataverse for Teams environments.

claims.claim: Further rollout mechanics for this export are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "work queue" "CSV" "export" "rollout" "scheduled" and "work queue" "CSV" "export" "automation center". Opened automation-center-overview and work-queues-manage; no export rollout mechanics beyond the supplied record.

claims.claim: Security roles are managed in Power Platform admin center through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments, and then select an environment from the list. ... Select Settings. ... Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. ... On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: The cited Dataverse reference documents the printed POST and @odata.id body for assigning a security role to a Microsoft Entra ID group user.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and api; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant or environment switch to enable or disable this CSV export is documented on the UI or automation surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate work queue CSV export disable enable setting Power Platform admin center PowerShell pac admin API; "work queue" "CSV export" "Power Platform API" "Dataverse" "pac admin". Read feature pages and returned PowerShell/reference excerpts; no switch.

claims.claim: Assigning security roles requires at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table.
claims.quote: To assign security roles to a user, you need to have the appropriate privileges (minimum privileges are Read and Assign on the Security Role table).

claims.claim: The System Administrator role has the required security-role assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Dataverse RBAC for limiting work queue use in API-based scenarios.
claims.quote: if you want to limit the use of work queues in cloud flow and API-based scenarios, you should use Dataverse RBAC to control access to the underlying tables.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Controlling read access to Work Queue and Work Queue Item tables is a documented way to limit visibility of their data in the automation center.
claims.quote: administrators can create custom security roles with row-level privileges to control the data users can view and interact with. ... Work Queue | prvReadworkqueue ... Work Queue Item | prvReadworkqueueitem

claims.claim: The feature produces a portable downloaded file rather than leaving the exported data solely in Dataverse.
